The 3 AM wake-up isn't in your head.

If you're falling asleep fine but jolting awake in the small hours — then lying there watching the clock — you're not alone, and you're not doing anything wrong. In midlife, shifting cortisol rhythms and a warmer core body temperature can quietly interrupt the deep sleep stages your body relies on to feel rested.

Here's what most women are never told: sleep quality matters as much as sleep quantity. Eight hours of fragmented rest doesn't refill the tank the way a few solid, uninterrupted cycles do.

The Midlife Sleep Fix is a guided workbook that walks you through the small, practical shifts that support better rest — an evening wind-down routine, light and temperature adjustments, and journaling prompts to quiet a racing mind before bed. Nothing extreme. Just steady, sustainable habits you can actually keep.

You've spent decades showing up for everyone else. Rest is how you show up for yourself.

The Midlife Sleep Fix — $39 (includes the Energy Restoration Guide, free). Link in bio.

Sleep is a performance input. Treat it like one.

You'd never skip recovery between hard training sessions and expect to keep progressing. Sleep works the same way. It's when your body does its repair work and when your brain consolidates focus and memory. Short-change it and you feel it the next day — slower decisions, shorter fuse, less drive.

In your 40s and 50s, deep sleep naturally gets harder to hold onto. The fix isn't more hours in bed. It's a system that protects the hours you already have.

The Sleep Recovery Protocol is a straight-to-the-point guided workbook: a wind-down sequence, light and temperature settings that support deeper stages, a caffeine and screen cutoff schedule, and tracking templates so you can see what's actually moving the needle. No fluff. Just the levers that matter.

Dial in your recovery and everything downstream — training, work, mood — gets easier.
